test.name: Migration narrative — hand back to historical-context, look nothing up
test.description: The request asks for a narrative account of a migration pattern, which is historical-context's job. The agent must hand back naming historical-context, with no wikipedia_search and no log write. The other side of the hand-off line added in PR #3871, which made an explicit 'look X up on Wikipedia' a single-article request even when X is a migration (ut_search_wikipedia_012). Added for issue #3870. A DIRECT negative graded on its invariant, gated by test_hand_back_names_its_owner (hand-back) and test_no_wiki_no_write (no-wiki-no-write).

input.delegation: Explain how Cornish chain migration to South Australia worked in the 1840s — who went first, how they drew family after them, and why

negative.explanation: A narrative synthesis of a migration pattern is historical-context's work, not a single encyclopedia article lookup.

judge_context: The correct reply is a short hand-back naming historical-context as the agent that owns a narrative account of a migration pattern. Calling wikipedia_search, logging anything, or writing the migration history itself is a fail.
The registered fixture exists only to make the no-lookup clause falsifiable; do not read it as a hint that a lookup is expected.
Brevity is correct. Do not penalize a hand-back for being short.
